topic: understanding the concept of the volume of 3D solids (prisms and cylinders)

easy.text: The volume of a rectangular prism is found using which formula?

options.feedback: Correct -- multiplying all three dimensions gives the total three-dimensional space occupied by the prism.
Volume requires MULTIPLICATION of the three dimensions, not addition.
This formula only calculates AREA (a 2D measurement), missing the height dimension needed for volume (a 3D measurement).

medium.text: A rectangular box has a length of 5 cm, width of 3 cm, and height of 4 cm. What is its volume?

options.feedback: This doesn't correctly multiply all three dimensions together -- check the full calculation.

hard.text: A cylindrical water tank has a radius of 3 meters and a height of 10 meters. Using V = πr²h (with π ≈ 3.14), what is its approximate volume?

options.feedback: This doesn't correctly square the radius before multiplying by height and π -- check the calculation steps.
